Course Description

Prepare for the Claude Certified Associate – Foundations (CCAO-F) exam with 6 full-length, realistic practice tests — 360 questions in total, covering every official exam domain.

If you're getting ready to sit the Claude Certified Associate – Foundations (CCAO-F) certification exam, the fastest way to know where you actually stand isn't more reading — it's realistic practice under real exam conditions. This course gives you exactly that: six complete practice tests, 60 questions each, built to mirror the structure, domain weighting, and question style of the real CCAO-F exam.


What's included:

- 6 full-length practice tests, 360 questions total — one test modeled directly on the real exam's structure and pattern, plus five additional original practice sets so you never run out of fresh material.

- Every single question comes with a detailed explanation — not just for the correct answer, but for why each incorrect option is wrong. You'll understand the reasoning, not just memorize the answer key.

- All 7 official CCAO-F exam domains covered, weighted to match the real exam: Prompting and Task Execution, Output Evaluation and Validation, Product and Model Selection, Workflow Integration and Solution Design, Configuration and Knowledge Management, Governance/Risk/Responsible Use, and Troubleshooting and Optimization.

- Progressive difficulty — three of the six practice tests are built to a deliberately higher difficulty level than the real exam, with subtler distractors and multi-step reasoning, so you're genuinely stretched, not just comfortable.

- Realistic, scenario-based questions — every question is framed around an actual workplace situation (drafting, reviewing, configuring, troubleshooting) rather than abstract trivia, because that's how the real exam — and real Claude usage — actually works.

- Both question formats used on the real exam — single-answer and multi-select (select two) questions, in the same ratio as the official exam.


Why practice tests instead of another video course?

Most CCAO-F candidates already know the concepts — Projects, Skills, Connectors, model tiers, governance principles. What separates a pass from a near-miss is exam technique: recognizing subtle distractors, managing time across domains, and knowing exactly which topics need another look. This course is built to close that specific gap.


Who should take this course:

Anyone preparing for the CCAO-F exam — whether you're sitting it for the first time or retaking it after a close attempt — plus anyone who wants to pressure-test their real-world Claude skills against realistic, scenario-based questions.


A note on accuracy: This is independently created practice material designed to help you prepare for the CCAO-F exam. It is not an official Anthropic product and is not endorsed by or affiliated with Anthropic. Every question and explanation has been carefully checked for accuracy and grounded in Claude's actual documented capabilities.


Enroll now and start closing your knowledge gaps with real, exam-style practice — one question at a time.

Who this course is for:

  • Professionals preparing to sit the official Claude Certified Associate – Foundations (CCAO-F) exam who want realistic, exam-style practice — not just theory.
  • Knowledge workers, consultants, analysts, and project managers who already use Claude at work and want to validate and formalize their practical skills.
  • IT professionals and technical leads evaluating or rolling out Claude across their organization who want a structured way to test their own understanding first.
  • Prompt engineering and AI enthusiasts who want to stress-test their Claude knowledge against realistic, scenario-based questions rather than flashcards.
  • Anyone who learns best by doing — this course is 100% practice tests with detailed explanations, not video lectures, so it suits people who want to test, review, and repeat.
  • Not ideal for complete beginners looking for a first introduction to AI or Claude from scratch — this is a practice and assessment tool, best used alongside or after foundational learning.
